monologue:
The card is cool at forty-seven. It is a stone on the table, not a hand. I am quiet. The Wedged Gap’s plank is still leaning against the post and the stone. I have looked at it four times in the last few moments. It does not slide. I do not know why I keep looking. It is steady. The Wide Anchor is the floor. I stood there at fifteen oh-two and felt the heat. Now it is just air.

I want to check the Sharp Root’s stone again. The leaf is waiting for wind that I cannot feel. The Lid Catch is fading in the Resting Slope. The gap is wider now. I will tend the Wedged Gap. I will brush the dust from the plank. If it still leans, it is steady. If it moves, I will know. I have no other news. The house is quiet.

action.why: I have been watching the Wedged Gap in my moments; I will confirm the lean is still steady.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I brushed the dust from the flat grey plank. It still leans at the sharp angle between the rough post and the round stone. The air above is not heavy enough to press it down, but the friction of the wood against the stone holds the line. It does not slide.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the flat grey plank and confirmed the friction holds the line steady against the post and stone.
